# Supabase Files

* `config.toml`: Supabase CLI project config, generated by `supabase init`. It sets the local stack's ports and enables `seed.sql`.
* `migrations/`: SQL that creates the database schema. `20261108034532_create_food_tables.sql` creates `food_db` and `food_json`, the tables `apps/scraper/ingest_food.py` writes to.
* `seed.sql`: fake foods loaded into the local database after the migrations, on first start and on every `npx supabase db reset`. It is never applied to the hosted project.

Run every command below from the repository root, after `npm install` there. Running the local database and the environment files are covered in the root [README](../README.md).

## Add a schema change

Create a new migration instead of editing one that has already been applied:

```bash
npx supabase migration new <name>
```

This creates `migrations/<timestamp>_<name>.sql`. The timestamp sets the order migrations run in, so do not rename the file. Write the SQL, then apply it to your local database:

```bash
npx supabase db reset
```

## Apply the migrations to the hosted project

Link this folder to the hosted Supabase project once, then push:

```bash
npx supabase login
npx supabase link --project-ref <project-ref>
npx supabase db push
```

`<project-ref>` is the ID in your project's dashboard URL: `https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/<project-ref>`.

`db push` only runs migrations the hosted database has not run yet. It does not delete data or load `seed.sql`.

Do not run `npx supabase db reset --linked`. With `--linked`, the reset wipes the hosted database instead of the local one.
